questions.text: Which HTML tag creates the largest heading?
questions.hint: Think about heading levels, where h1 is the most important.

questions.text: What does CSS stand for?
questions.hint: It's a style sheet language used for describing presentation.

questions.text: Which is the best practice for adding CSS to an HTML page?
questions.hint: Separation of concerns - keep content and presentation separate.

questions.text: In the CSS Box Model, which property controls space outside the element's border?
questions.hint: It creates space between elements.

questions.text: Which animation principle states almost all living motion follows a curved path?
questions.hint: Think about natural movement - it's rarely in a straight line.

questions.text: A character crouches before jumping. Which animation principle does this demonstrate?
questions.hint: It's a preparation for the main action.

questions.text: Which animation principle do CSS ease-in and ease-out properties directly mimic?
questions.hint: It's about acceleration and deceleration.

questions.text: Which design principle explains why a bright button stands out from surrounding body text?
questions.hint: It's about making elements different to draw attention.

questions.text: The 60-30-10 rule is associated with which design principle?
questions.hint: It's a rule for balancing colors.

questions.text: A web layout uses a 12-column invisible skeleton for consistent spacing. Which principle is this?
questions.hint: It's about organizing content in a structured layout.

questions.text: Which best describes a wireframe?
questions.hint: It's a basic, low-detail sketch.

questions.text: What is the key difference between a mockup and a prototype?
options: Mockup has color; prototype does not
Mockup is interactive; prototype is static
Mockup is static; prototype is interactive
questions.hint: Mockups are visual, prototypes are functional.

questions.text: Which JavaScript method selects an element by ID and changes its content?
questions.hint: Used to change the HTML content inside an element.

questions.text: Which design principle states: "If it only works for some users, it isn't finished"?
questions.hint: It's about designing for all users, regardless of ability.

questions.text: The most important animation principle - gives an object the illusion of weight and flexibility while keeping volume constant.
questions.hint: Think of a bouncing ball.

questions.text: Presents one clear focal point so the audience cannot miss the main idea; the silhouette reads instantly even in shadow.
questions.hint: It's about directing attention.

questions.text: A minor motion that adds richness without pulling focus from the main action - like a tail swishing while a character walks.
questions.hint: It's a smaller movement that supports the main one.

questions.text: The animation principle referring to the overall quality that makes a character pleasant and interesting to watch, even a villain.
questions.hint: It's about charisma and charm.

questions.text: Related items placed close together; unrelated items given space - tells the viewer what belongs together without labels or borders.
questions.hint: Grouping by closeness.

questions.text: Reusing the same fonts, colors, and button styles throughout an interface so users only have to learn how something works once.
questions.hint: It's about being predictable.

questions.text: Generous empty space that improves readability and focus - the fastest way to make a design feel premium.
questions.hint: Also known as negative space.

questions.text: A high-fidelity, static design with full colors, real typography, and images - but no interactivity.
questions.hint: Looks like the final product but doesn't function.

questions.text: The CSS selector syntax used to target an element with a unique identifier (e.g., id="box").
questions.hint: It uses the hash symbol.

questions.text: The stage in the design workflow that comes after a wireframe but before a prototype.
questions.hint: It's the visual design phase.
